Ask about this server in plain language — Codex investigates using a handful of read-only Docker tools (images, volumes, containers, disk usage). Nothing is ever deleted or changed; it only looks.

Deployments

Clone a GitHub repo onto a VPS, write a .env from your variables, and run docker compose up -d --build — or leave the repo URL blank to drive an existing directory (e.g. one your own CI pipeline already deploys) as-is. 


            

          

        


        
        

          

            
            

              
Migrate a Compose stack

              

                Moves a docker-compose stack from one VPS to another: compose file,
                env files, and named volumes. The source is never shut down by
                the app — you'll do that yourself after verifying the target.
              

              
              
              
              
              
              
              
              

                Required when the SSH user can't write to the target compose dir,
                or when docker isn't accessible without sudo. Assumes passwordless
                sudo (or root) — if sudo is refused, the error is shown as-is.
              

              

                
              

              

            


            
            

              
Multiple stacks found

              

                This folder has no compose file of its own, but its subdirectories do.
                Pick which stacks to migrate — each goes to
                /<name> on the target.

Remove a stack

              

                Tears down a docker-compose stack on this VPS: docker compose down,
                and optionally its named volumes, images, and the stack directory. External
                volumes and networks are left untouched.
              

              
              
              

                
              

              

            


            
            

              
Confirm removal

              

              
What to remove

              
              
              
              
⚠ This is irreversible. Type the stack folder name to confirm.

Expose a service on a domain

              

                Routes a compose service to a hostname with automatic HTTPS via your
                caddy-docker-proxy, by adding labels through a compose
                override file — your own compose file is left untouched.
              

              
Click “Detect proxy” to check this host.

                Point the domain at this VPS. Provision a database

              

                Stands up a managed database as its own docker-compose stack. It then appears
                in the Databases tab and can be backed up. No host port is exposed by default —
                access is over docker exec.
